name: The Corponation Catechism
creator: Anonymous (attributed to 'Blessed Tunde')
description: Formatted precisely like a religious instruction manual — numbered articles, call-and-response sections, a glossary of 'sacred terms' — this text systematically parodies the ideological apparatus of corponation citizenship, replacing words like 'employee' with 'devotee' and 'quarterly earnings' with 'divine harvest.' Beneath the savage humor is a rigorous political-economic analysis of how corponations manufacture consent through culture, housing, healthcare, and education. The authorship attribution to 'Blessed Tunde' is widely understood as a collective pseudonym.
medium: physical zine (multiple underground print runs) and encrypted neural feed
cultural_impact: Estimated to be the most-reproduced underground text in GLMZ history; the phrase 'praise the harvest' entered Shelf vernacular as a bitter ironic idiom and is now used even by people who've never read the source.
controversy: At least three people have been arrested under corporate IP law for distributing copies; Helix Consolidated's legal division has spent significant resources trying to identify 'Blessed Tunde' without success.
story_hooks: Someone claiming to be the original author of The Corponation Catechism has reached out to a journalist — but the claim is unverifiable and the timing is suspicious.
A new edition has appeared with three additional chapters that read differently in style and may constitute a deliberate ideological distortion of the original.
A Tier 4 corporate attorney has been secretly distributing copies inside her firm, and someone has noticed.
